name: CFS Recovery (Recovery School / Recovery Academy / Recovery Platinum)
founders: Miguel Bautista (reportedly Canada-based; former athlete and video-business owner who reports recovering from self-described CFS, ill 2017 to 2019; no clinical credentials)
founded_year_range: 2021 (the About page timeline says 'CFS Recovery Founded' in 2021; the founder was ill 2017-2019)
cost_summary: Monthly subscription, verified Oct 2026. Recovery School is US$47/mo (self-paced plus a weekly group call). Recovery Academy is US$297/mo (up to 7 live group calls a week). Recovery Platinum is 1:1 coaching, priced by application, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. All tiers can be cancelled at any time. A free assessment and a free training are offered. A year on Academy costs about US$3.5k.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
limbic system impairment / amygdala threat conditioning
mechanism_summary: The program treats these conditions as one nervous system "stuck, not broken" in a chronic stress/threat response. A trigger (infection, stress, overload) switches on an alarm that stays on. The resulting real symptoms are then read as danger, which keeps the loop going, with fear of symptoms as the key maintaining factor. A "stress threshold/bucket" (allostatic load) model has all stressors filling a single tank. Supporting language includes sympathetic overactivity, a non-resetting HPA axis, central sensitisation, vagal brain-immune signalling and neuroplastic reversibility. It is one mechanism for ME/CFS, long COVID, fibromyalgia and POTS; individualisation is through a proprietary assessment, not by disease.
techniques: cognitive reframing of symptoms as safe
Nervous System Health Assessment and SF-36 progress tracking
mainstream_notes: The site says CFS Recovery is a coaching and educational company and that its staff "are not doctors". Its coaches are lay recovered patients with in-house training. There is no health-system, guideline or insurer uptake. The only named physician endorser is one functional-medicine MD (Scott Resnick); the other professional quotes are Trustpilot reviews.
insurance_notes: It is a coaching subscription. The home page and FAQ mention no insurance or HSA billing.
controversy: The company advertises in-house "aggregate" SF-36 gains (+18% at 6 months, +40% at 12 months) with no N, control group, attrition data or definition of the metric. It sets them beside uncited 'published trial' benchmarks (standard care 5-10%, exercise 10-15%, CBT 8-12%). Its self-reported figures are internally inconsistent: 50+ vs 100+ hours of video, and 2,000+ clients helped vs 'hundreds' recovered. The 'Physician Endorsed' badge rests on one functional-medicine MD, and testimonials are not independent. It shares the criticisms made of the whole limbic-retraining genre: ME/CFS advocates object to the stress/fear framing, to the risk of post-exertional crashes from 'expansion' and to open-ended subscription costs sold to a vulnerable group. Coaches are unlicensed.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 2,000-3,000 paying clients (company claim of 2,000+), plus perhaps tens of thousands of YouTube viewers. Core reach is about 10^3.4.
popularity.method_notes: Web search was exhausted in both the research and fact-check sessions, so Reddit, Wayback, Google Trends and YouTube subscriber data were not retrieved. The trajectory is inferred from the stated 2021 founding, the growth from a solo offer to a multi-coach tiered subscription, and the self-reported 2,000+ clients. Reach_log10 rests on an unaudited company claim and is uncertain.
